utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: When you were in the field as a monitor, were you looking to see whether or not the Geneva Convention was being applied by the conflicting forces?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you didn't have -- you didn't bear in mind at all whether there were infractions of the Geneva Convention?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- no. There were -- it was against the Geneva Convention. That's what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: No, my question -- it maybe you're confused.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infractions?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Crimes.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crimes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Violations.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crimes -- yes, there were crimes of the Geneva Convention.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, would you expect the officers of the conflicting forces to be aware of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this a cross-examination or a re-examination? Mr. Flynn is leading the witness on very important matters here. I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to be as patient and move the witness on as -- my first question was very fair. He was speaking specifically about the HVO. My colleagues constantly interrupt. I'm now trying to bring him bit by bit to the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We have to interrupt [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Flynn, but I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please, Mr. Scott. I notice that ever have I time we are -- whenever we are in redirect there are always incidents. So -- always. So in order to avoid this, we have to proceed in a professional manner. We have to try to avoid to ask leading questions. Up until now, up until line 4 of page 93, there were no leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy rose to his feet after line 6. Maybe the problem started there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Flynn was asking -- conducting a perfectly reasonable redirect examination, and then, as so often happens, and I submit that it's an intentional run at the clock at the end of the day, these harassing interventions start that are not fair. They're not reasonable. Then Your Honour intervened, and I have to say and with the greatest of respect, the objections that Your Honour made and I'm talking, Mr. President, could have all been made to the same questions put by the Defence. But all of a sudden everything took a complete turn in a different direction when the Prosecution started putting reasonable follow-up questions to the witness, and then Mr. Flynn, following the president's direction, started going down a specific set of questions to lay the foundation that you directed him to lay. So it's completely -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, but it's not appropriate. Now, Mr. Flynn should be given the chance to conduct a re-examination, and I have to disagree with my colleagues, but you know, it seems the rules change. As soon as we're on redirect the rules completely change and all the questions that the Defence were able to put and assume and presume about the HVO and what they did or didn't know and what they could have -- none of these things were put to them, and when Mr. Flynn gets back on his feet it's a whole different set of rules. I object to that. It's not fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may make one brief observation in order to assist everyone. Mr. Flynn was asking a very general question over a span of time of two, three years. Obviously it was a general question. It was objected to. Perhaps if Mr. Flynn would get to the specific question that he wanted to ask in that area then we could just move along. I understand where he wants to go, but it has to be specific to the time, place, and perhaps -- I think that's -- that's where all of the objections came up on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think it is absolutely reasonable to go from a general to a specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And I really doubt whether it was justified to cut off at the general question and to want to refuse a general question. I don't think that was a just intervention that was justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't intervene, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No, it wasn't you. But it was the side you are talking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm just trying to move the process along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, on redirect -- and I apologise to my colleague for intervening, I don't mean any offence to my colleague in taking my feet, but Mr. Flynn was specifically responding to questions put during cross-examination about the responsibility of a commander and very general questions that were put by the Defence, and if we need to go back and to go through the transcript to find them, we can do that tomorrow, but there were a number of questions. How long does it take to create an army? Well, maybe 10 years. Well, those were all general questions, and Mr. Flynn asked a reasonable follow-up question: Well, Mr. Gerritsen what do you do in that situation? What are the responsibility and -- those are fair questions. But what happens, Your Honour, in response to what you've said is that we get up on redirect and it becomes this constant series of harassment, and then when Mr. Flynn tries to ask the questions that the President asked him to ask it just continues, and we have to object to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to say one sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn, please proceed. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I'll try and shorten it, Your Honour and I'll try and be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: The circumstances in which you found yourself in Gornji Vakuf AOR in the summer of 1993, can you tell us, did you see any efforts by senior commanders to discipline their troops if they did not obey their orders? ?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't personally see these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Would you have expected them to do so --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: -- given the circumstances they found themselves and the events which were happening?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions. Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my redirect. I'm sure up join with me, Lieutenant Colonel Gerritsen is retiring from the military tomorrow, and from the Prosecution we certainly wish him all the best and congratulate him for his many years' service.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise but perhaps it would be very valuable if the witness could explain to us how he could see an HVO commander endeavour to do something with respect to soldiers who engaged it in some unlawful act. How could he be expected to see something like that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, but on line 16 the witness said that he himself did not see anything, and that's written on line 16. Colonel -- Mr. Praljak, we've concluded the hearing of this witness. Thank you very much on behalf of my colleagues and myself for coming here to testify for the third time in your life before this Tribunal, and I would like to congratulate you and to wish you good luck in your military career. And that being said, I would like to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly. Mr. Registrar, can we please move into a private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Without giving any names, we have a witness tomorrow. According to our calculations, unless I am mistaken, for the Defence cross-examination they will have one hour and 17 minutes. I do not have the precise number of minutes for each counsel, between 5D, 6D, and 3D. So if tomorrow you haven't agreed amongst yourselves, we will divide that time in three. So we have exactly 1 hour and 17 minutes left. This is for you. And then after that Judges will put some additional questions. Then there's the redirect, and so on and so forth. I am saying this so that everybody is perfectly informed. Ms. Nozica? Yes, I may have forgotten 2D.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Thank you. For the record, I'd just like to say that I was interrupted halfway through my cross-examination, but we shall agree amongst ourselves how much time each of us will have with respect to the remaining time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It would be best if you could agree amongst yourselves. I prefer that solution, of course, rather than deciding for you how much time is allowed to each Defence counsel. We only intervene when you cannot agree on something. The best would be to come tomorrow and say 1D needs this much time, 2D this much time, et cetera. So you should agree amongst yourselves, and please let us know how you have agreed on the time. It's not very complicated. Witness is coming to testify. You can see who will put the questions first, so I think that it's not too difficult to divvy up the time amongst yourselves. If not, the Judges will do that for you. As you will know, the hearing stands adjourned, and we will resume tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.56 p.m.,
